answer: Age in the trust hierarchy is bought with per-identity verified output rather than with elapsed time, so an operator cannot batch his accounts through a queue and must run each one through genuine, individually verified work. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. The ember is the attested output, the ridge the stranger who checks it, and the umber the tier the pair unlocks; the ember is per identity, the ridge cannot be the farm's own, and the umber is what waiting alone cannot buy. Each head also needs a stranger to attest that work.
